summary: Ep 10 'Thank You' is NOT a recap and not a free-standing anime interlude: it is an adaptation of the light novel's own short stories. The 86 fandom wiki's per-episode 'adaptation' field (the same field that reads 'Light Novel Volume 1: Chapter 7' for ep 9 and 'Volume 1 Ch 7 + Volume 2 Ch 2' for ep 11) reads for ep 10: 'Light Novel Volume 10: Varlet, Banks of Lethe, & Fido' plus the side story 'For Nameless Soldiers Have No Graves'. Volume 10 (Ep.10 -Fragmental Neoteny-, Dengeki Bunko, released 2021-06-10, two days BEFORE this episode aired) is a numbered volume of the source series - a compilation of previously and newly written short stories - so this material is the source, not an anime invention. TV Tropes' LN-reader adaptation log independently breaks the episode down the same way: the front half (river rest, fishing, the abandoned Giadian town and zoo) is the short story 'By the Lethe River' = ch 8 of Volume 10; the back half (Fido's memory montage) is built on the 'Fido' short story plus the 4-page side story bundled with manga volume 1; and 'the only thing directly taken from the main story novels is the last 30 seconds of the episode, which shows Fido destroyed as the start of Volume 2 Chapter 2.' The one dissent is ANN's episode review (Callum May), which calls it an 'anime original episode' - written by an anime-only reviewer two days after the source volume shipped in Japanese; it is a perception, not a source claim. Under T28 the episode's whole plot IS those short stories, so this clears the materiality bar comfortably: canon, with a side_story annotation because the bulk is the LN's short-story volume rather than mainline volume progression.

standings.note: Adapts light novel material, not anime-original: LN volume 10 'Fragmental Neoteny' short stories ('The Banks of Lethe' = vol 10 ch 8; 'Fido') + the 4-page Asato-written side story 'For Nameless Soldiers Have No Graves' bundled with manga vol 1, closing on the opening of LN vol 2 ch 2 (Fido's destruction). Two independent sources agree (fandom per-episode adaptation field; TV Tropes' LN-reader adaptation log). Volume unit, no chapter anchor claimed - the series has no anchors and LN volumes are the instrument; 'chapters: none' means no chapter mapping, NOT no source content. Repair of the stored filler standing (T27 default) to canon. Dissent recorded: ANN's episode-10 review calls it an 'anime original episode' (anime-only reviewer, 2021-06-14).

annotations.note: The episode's body is the source's SIDE stories (LN vol 10's short-story collection + the manga-vol-1 bonus story by Asato Asato), not mainline volume progression; only the final ~30 seconds is mainline (start of vol 2 ch 2). Mainline position is unaffected: ep 9 and ep 11 both sit in vol 1 ch 7, and ep 11 is the one that moves into vol 2 ch 2.

repairs.why: Not anime-original: it adapts LN vol 10's short stories ('By the Lethe River' ch 8, 'Fido'), the manga-vol-1 bonus side story, and the opening of vol 2 ch 2. AFL's 'anime canon' tag here reflects 'not a mainline volume', not 'no source'.

structure.notes: Our 23 rows = the 23 TV episodes only (S1 eps 1-11 = rows 1-11; Part 2 eps 12-23 = rows 12-23), which matches the fandom episode list and Wikipedia. Broadcast ALSO included four 'Special Edition' programmes that we do NOT carry as rows: SE1 'Coquelicots Blooming Across the Battlefield' (2021-06-26, after ep 11), SE2 'Visual Commentary Special' (2021-11-13), SE3 'If There's Something Worth Dying For' (2021-11-27), SE4 'At Least Try To Be Human' (2022-03-05). These are recap/commentary specials; if they are ever ingested they would be filler + abridged (recap) and would shift every row after ep 11 - do not add them without renumbering. No ep 0. Ep 10 is a regular numbered TV episode, not an OVA or special.

flags_for_sean: Split perception on 86 ep 10: fandom + TV Tropes document it as an adaptation of LN vol 10's short stories, while ANN's contemporaneous review calls it 'anime original' (https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/review/86/episode-10/.173902). I recommend canon + side_story; the vol-10 stories are numbered source material (Dengeki Bunko 'Ep.10 -Fragmental Neoteny-') and the episode's plot IS them.

If side-story-sourced rows should carry a volume-level position rather than 'none', 86 ep 10 is the test case: the mainline reading position at ep 10 is still vol 1 ch 7 / vol 2 ch 2 (ep 11 carries that).
